'''Jon Ogborn''' {{postnom|country=GBR|HonFInstP}} is a physicist and former Professor of Science Education at the [[UCL Institute of Education|Institute of Education]] in the [[University of London]], and a former Professor of Science Education at the [[University of Sussex]].<ref name=icpe>{{cite web|url=https://web.phys.ksu.edu/icpe/Medals/Citations/ogborn.htm|title=''Citation for the Presentation of the ICPE Medal to Professor Jon Michael Ogborn of the Institute of Education, University of London Tokyo 2006''|website=International Commission on Physics Education|access-date=8 January 2021}}</ref> With [[Paul Black (educational researcher)|Paul Black]], Ogborn co-developed the [[Nuffield Foundation]] [[A-level]] physics qualification during the late 1960s and in the 1990s led the project to develop a new Advanced Physics A-level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/honorary-fellowship/our-honorary-fellows/professor-jon-ogborn#gref|title=''Professor Jon Ogborn, Honorary Fellow''|website=Institute of Physics|access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref> He is Professor Emeritus at the [[University of London]] [[UCL Institute of Education|Institute of Education]].

==Early career==
Ogborn attended [[Richard Hale School|Hertford Grammar School]],<ref>''Hertford Mercury'' Friday 6 March 1953, page 4</ref> leaving in 1953,<ref>''Hertford Mercury'' Friday 28 August 1953, page 7</ref> before attending the [[University of Cambridge]], where he gained his degree in Natural Sciences. He followed this by achieving a [[Post Graduate Certificate of Education]] at [[UCL Institute of Education|Institute of Education]] in the [[University of London]]. Ogborn's first role was as a Physics teacher at [[William Ellis School]] in [[Highgate]], [[London]]. Within a few years, Ogborn had progressed to Head of Science at [[The John Roan School|Roan Grammar School]] in [[Greenwich]] before leaving to join the academic staff at [[University of Worcester|Worcester College of Higher Education]].<ref name=icpe/>

While at [[University of Worcester|Worcester College of Higher Education]] during the late 1960s, he was selected to develop the [[Nuffield Foundation]] [[A-Level]] Physics programme with [[Paul Black (educational researcher)|Paul Black]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chilton-computing.org.uk/acl/associates/users/black.htm|title=''Paul Black and Jon Ogborn, Nuffield Advanced Physics Project''|website=Chilton Computing|access-date=5 February 2021}}</ref> In 1971, Ogborn returned to London to work as a Senior Research Fellow, then as Reader in Physics Education at [[Chelsea College of Science and Technology]].<ref name=icpe/> During the early 1970s Ogborn was the Project co-ordinator for ''The Higher Education Learning Project in Physics'' which was funded by the [[Nuffield Foundation]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/03075077712331376453?journalCode=cshe20|title=''P.J. Black & Jon Ogborn (1977) Inter-university collaboration in methods of teaching science, Studies in Higher Education, 2:2, 149-159, DOI:10.1080/03075077712331376453''|issue=2 |pages=149–159 |journal=Studies in Higher Education|date=January 1977 |volume=2 |doi=10.1080/03075077712331376453|access-date=8 February 2021|last1=Black |first1=P. J. |last2=Ogborn |first2=Jon |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1975 Ogborn was selected by [[György Marx]] to be involved in the second Danube Seminar returning for further seminars over further years.<ref>{{citation|title=Groupe Internationale pour la Recherche sur l'Enseignement de la Physique, Newsletter 47, January 2003}}</ref><ref name=icpe/>

==Later career==
In 1984 Ogborn left [[Chelsea College of Science and Technology]] to become the Professor of Science Education at [[UCL Institute of Education|Institute of Education]] in the [[University of London]],<ref name=exp/> a position he held until 1997, when he joined the [[University of Sussex]] in the same position of Professor of Science Education.  He retired from this position in 2001, becoming Professor Emeritus of Science Education at [[UCL Institute of Education|Institute of Education]].<ref name=icpe/>

Between 1992 and 1995, Ogborn worked on the [[Nuffield Foundation]] funded project ''Teaching about why things change'' with Richard Boohan, developing ''Energy and Change'', a publication of three booklets to make thermodynamic ideas accessible to school students.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stem.org.uk/resources/collection/3624/energy-and-change|title=Energy and Change|website=STEM Learning|access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tes.com/news/break-down-energy-barrier%3f|title=''Break down the energy barrier''|publisher=TES|date=3 January 1997|access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref> Between February and March 1993, Ogborn was an Osher Fellow.<ref name=exp>{{cite web|url=https://www.exploratorium.edu/collaborations/oshers/jon-ogborn|title=Jon Ogborn, Osher Fellow, February and March, 1993|website=Exploratorium|date=8 January 2013 |access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref> In 1997 he was selected to lead the Advancing Physics [[A-Level]] project funded by the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{citation|title=''Jon Ogborn, October 2016, Physics Education 51 030107''}}</ref><ref name=icpe/>

Internationally Ogborn has completed research with Groupe Internationale de Recherche sur l’Enseignement de la Physique, the European Science Education Research Association and the [[European Union]].<ref name=icpe/> During his membership with the International Commission on Physics Education he edited the second edition of their publication ''Physics Now''.<ref name=icpe/>

==Awards==
In 1973, Ogborn jointly won the [[Institute of Physics Awards|Lawrence Bragg Medal and Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold-medals/lawrence-bragg-medal-and-prize-recipients#gref|title=''Lawrence Bragg Medal and Prize recipients''|website=Institute of Physics|access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref> with [[Paul Black (educational researcher)|Paul Black]]. Ogborn has been made an Honorary Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]], and was a medallist and an Honorary Member of the Roland Eötvös Physical Society of Hungary.<ref name=icpe/> In 2006 he won the ICPE Medal for his contributions to physics education, ''"which have been outstanding in their nature and international in their scope and influence"''.<ref name=icpe/>

==Personal life==
As a child Ogborn lived at Carbone Hill at [[Cuffley]], with his brother David and sisters Ruth and Elizabeth and Mary, and father Maurice.<ref>''Hertford Mercury'' Friday 10 April 1953, page 5</ref> Ruth married in March 1972 at [[Northaw]]. Ruth attended [[Presdales School|Ware Grammar School]].<ref>''Surrey Advertiser'' Friday 31 March 1972, page 17</ref>

Ogborn has been married three times. His had three children with his first wife, Jane Mackereth. They divorced in the 1970s. His second wife, Professor Joan Bliss, died in 2011. He has subsequently remarried. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2011/jun/08/joan-bliss-obituary|title=''Joan Bliss Obituary''|work=The Guardian|date=8 June 2011|access-date=6 February 2021}}</ref> Ogborn and Bliss had co-written articles together.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=x7_vAAAAMAAJ|title=''Students Reactions to Undergraduate Science''|author=John Ogborn, Joan Bliss|publisher=Heinemann Educational for Nuffield Foundation Volume 4|year=1977|isbn=9780435695835|access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=''Force and motion from the beginning'', December 1994, Learning and Instruction 4(1):7–25 DOI: 10.1016/0959-4752(94)90016-7|doi=10.1016/0959-4752(94)90016-7}}</ref>

==Selected writings==
* 2003 - ''Soft matter: Food for thought'', December 2003, Physics Education, 39(1):45, {{doi|10.1088/0031-9120/39/1/001}} 
* 2005 - ''40 Years of Curriculum Development'', January 2005, In book: Research and the Quality of Science Education (pp.57-65, {{doi|10.1007/1-4020-3673-6_5}} 
* 2005 - ''Introducing relativity: Less may be more'', April 2005, Physics Education, 40(3):213, {{doi|10.1088/0031-9120/40/3/001}} 
* 2008 - ''Should science courses be context-led?'' - EIC, The Royal Society of Chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edu.rsc.org/opinion/should-science-courses-be-context-led/2021022.article|title=''Should science courses be context-led''|publisher=EIC - The Royal Society of Chemistry|date=1 March 2008|access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref>
* 2008 - ''A Future for Modelling in Science Education'', June 2008, Journal of Computer Assisted Learning, 6(2):103 - 112, {{doi|10.1111/j.1365-2729.1990.tb00355.x}}
